svg.title: A correct mroute only proves the control plane: the data plane needs replication resources of its own
svg.desc: Left panel: the control plane holds the (S,G) entry, the incoming interface and the outgoing interface list, all visible in show ip mroute and all correct. Right panel: the data plane needs a hardware entry per replication, TCAM space, and per-line-card replication capacity, none of which appear in the control plane view. A middle band lists the four places the two planes disagree: TCAM exhausted so the entry stays software-switched, one line card with an older microcode, an outgoing interface list wider than the replication engine supports, and a policer that drops silently. A bottom band gives the three commands that separate the planes.
svg.text: Two planes, two answers to "is it working"
Multicast forwarding is state plus hardware. The state can be perfect while the hardware quietly refuses to hold it.
CONTROL PLANE
show ip mroute says everything is fine
Incoming interface: GigabitEthernet0/1, RPF nbr 10.0.0.2
Outgoing interface list:
GigabitEthernet0/2, Forward, 00:42:11/00:03:12
GigabitEthernet0/3, Forward, 00:42:11/00:03:12
The entry exists, RPF is correct, the OIL is right.
Not one line of this output proves a packet left.
DATA PLANE
What the entry actually needs
1. A hardware (S,G) entry, not just a software one
2. A replication slot per outgoing interface
3. TCAM space in the region reserved for multicast
4. Enough fabric bandwidth to copy the packet N times
Miss any of the four and the traffic falls back to slow
path or is dropped, with the control plane unchanged.
FOUR PLACES THE TWO PLANES DISAGREE
TCAM exhausted
Entry 8,193 works, entry 8,194 is software
switched and cannot keep up. Symptom: the
newest channel is the one that stutters.
Mixed line cards
One card on older microcode has a lower
replication limit. Symptom: one floor fails.
OIL wider than the engine
Some platforms cap the fan-out per entry
(for example 16 or 32 copies). Symptom:
large branches lose a few ports, silently.
A policer on the path
A copy drops at a rate limit that counted only
unicast. Symptom: quality drops at peak only.
So compare the two
show ip mroute count
show platform hardware ... mroute
show interface ... | i rate
Software count minus hardware count is
the number of entries quietly failing.
Acceptance rule
Never accept "the mroute is there" as proof of delivery. Prove it with an egress counter on the last hop, at the busiest minute of the day.
